phase: 36 — proof that a selector-level QA scope fix is safe (MEASUREMENT ONLY, nothing modified)
harness: chapter/qa-p36-scope.html — runs the UNMODIFIED qa-engine, rebuilds its exact node list, then partitions the real findings by whether the finding’s node is a colorWordsIn decorative span. qa-engine.js was never edited; the selector change is applied only as a post-hoc partition of genuine engine output.

step1_distinction.whyReliable: colorWordsIn has EXACTLY two call sites in the entire codebase (chapter-app.js:3050 exercise mcq, :3349 reading-question mcq). Both are colorWordsIn(b.querySelector('.de')) where b is el('button', { class: 'mcq-option' }). Therefore every decorative span has a button.mcq-option ancestor by construction, and no wrapWordsIn span can have one (wrapWordsIn’s own TreeWalker rejects text inside LINK_EXCLUDE, whose first entry is "button").
step1_distinction.censusEvidence: grep for colorWordsIn returns 3 hits: the definition at :2928 and the two call sites. No third caller exists.

rejectedAlternatives.why: explicitly excluded by the brief and not stable
not expressible as a DOM selector; listeners are invisible to querySelectorAll
that marker distinguishes in-popup links, not decorative ones — normal prose links also lack it

step1_distinction.confidence: PROVEN — the distinction follows from an exhaustive call-site census, not from sampling

step2_step3_step4_measurement.exactMatchToPrediction: the 14 HCM dropped are exactly the 14 G-A occurrences named in P30/P31, and the 11 RCB dropped are exactly their co-located records. No other code lost a single finding.

step5_genuineCasesRetained.pureControl: a1-1-alphabet 0 before, 0 after — no false drops in a clean chapter
step5_genuineCasesRetained.nonHcmCodesUntouched: PARADIGM_CLASS_MISMATCH 5→5, CASE_COLLISION_CAPITALISED 4→4, NO_POPUP 1→1, CASE_COLLISION_LOWERCASE 1→1 — identical before and after
step5_genuineCasesRetained.noGenuineWrapWordsInFindingLost: PROVEN across all 12 chapters: every dropped finding sits on a node with a button.mcq-option ancestor, and 242 decorative nodes were present while only 25 findings existed on them

basis: the distinction is exhaustive by construction (2 call sites, both inside button.mcq-option), not statistical
measured, not assumed: 25 findings dropped, and they are precisely the predicted 14 HCM + 11 RCB
four control chapters covering all three genuine HCM groups lost nothing
caveats: b2-16 retains a NO_POPUP finding. That finding is NOT on a decorative node, so it survives correctly — but it is worth noting that if a future change made the engine skip decorative nodes at SELECTION time rather than filtering findings afterwards, occurrence indices would shift corpus-wide, exactly as seen in P22/P23. A post-selection filter avoids that; a pre-selection skip does not.

this phase measured 12 chapters, not 259. The corpus-wide effect is expected to be −14 HCM / −11 RCB because those are the only known decorative findings, but a full sweep would be required to confirm no other chapter has decorative findings.
step6_decision.recommendedShape: exclude nodes with a button.mcq-option ancestor from the QA node list, or equivalently suppress findings on them. NOT IMPLEMENTED.

impactRestatement.measuredExactly: 14 HCM and 11 RCB dropped across the 7 affected chapters
impactRestatement.interpretation: these were QA artefacts on decorative spans, not learner-facing defects (P35). Removing them reduces the corpus HCM population from 37 to 23 and RCB from 1020 to 1009, subject to full-sweep confirmation.
